title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync to check onboarding progress and environment readiness. Customer completed initial VPC peering and service account work but still needs KMS access and a couple infra tickets. SE reviewed preliminary latency/cost numbers from hosted vs dedicated profiles and proposed next benchmark windows. Action items agreed: Redwood to share security pack and updated benchmark runbook, Nexa to open KMS access ticket and provide sample prompt set. Plan: full benchmark next Tue followed by a canary deploy if numbers align.
next_steps: Redwood to send security and SOC2 docs by 2026-02-19
SE to share benchmark runbook and host/dedicated perf matrix by 2026-02-19
NexaHealth to open KMS access request and assign IAM role by 2026-02-20
action_items: Jordan Lee - Send security pack + SOC2 summary - Due: 2026-02-19
Priya Nair - Share benchmark runbook and perf matrix (hosted vs dedicated) - Due: 2026-02-19
Liam O'Connor - Open KMS access ticket and attach sample service account logs - Due: 2026-02-20
Sophie Grant - Provide 500 sample prompts and expected answer criteria - Due: 2026-02-20
Carlos Mendez - Confirm RBAC mapping for Redwood service account - Due: 2026-02-20
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give it a few secs for folks to pop in. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE. Priya is our SE.
[00:10] Priya Nair: Hi all. Quick agenda: onboarding status, infra blockers, review preliminary perf numbers, plan benchmark.
[00:18] Carlos Mendez: Hey Jordan, hey Priya. We have Sophie and Liam on — Anita from security will join in a few. We're at the point where VPC peering is done, cross-account role is set up, but KMS still pending.
[00:28] Jordan Lee: Great, that's progress. Liam, can you quickly confirm the peering details? Any IP ranges blocked?
[00:35] Liam O'Connor: Sure — peering established between our VPC and the Redwood endpoint VPC, routes added. We had to adjust our egress rules for the 10.3.0.0/16 range, there was one hiccup with our firewall rule that blocked 443 to the Redwood egress IP, but that's fixed.
[00:48] Priya Nair: Excellent. From Redwood side we validated connectivity earlier this morning, we saw successful health checks from the canary host. The missing piece is KMS access — we need a key alias and IAM permission so the private deployment can unwrap tokens.
[01:05] Anita Rao: On that — security wants to validate key policy and rotation schedule. We prefer customer-managed keys; can Redwood support a CMK in our account?
[01:14] Jordan Lee: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS/HSM keys for Private deployments. The typical pattern we use is a service account with kms:Decrypt only on the key alias, and we provide a sample IAM policy. We'll send the template after the call.
[01:27] Carlos Mendez: Ok, good. Next — perf numbers. Priya, you had some initial hosted vs dedicated latency/cost ballpark?
[01:34] Priya Nair: Right. We ran a lightweight smoke on hosted and a dedicated profile. Caveat: this was limited to short sequences and synthetic prompts. Hosted median tail latency was ~220ms per token at 16k context with our baseline model; dedicated with the reserved GPU profile showed ~160ms per token but higher throughput and predictable p99. Cost per 1k tokens was roughly 30% higher on dedicated in our config because of reserved overhead, but that gap narrows at scale with batching.
[01:55] Sophie Grant: Sorry, 220ms per token — is that end-to-end or token generation time? We're trying to understand user-facing latency for our chat UI.
[02:03] Priya Nair: Good question. That's server-side token generation — includes model execution but not client-side network jitter. For a 40-token response you'd see ~8.8s server-side on hosted in that synthetic test, though with streaming and prefix caching typical user flows that trims a lot.
[02:20] Liam O'Connor: 8.8 seconds is too long for our support triage use case. What tuning levers do we have? Quantization? Smaller model variants?
[02:27] Priya Nair: Yes — options: 1) quantized weights on dedicated for lower latency/cost, 2) model distillation to a smaller variant for low-latency paths, 3) batching and prefix caching for repeated prompts, 4) adjusting temperature/top-p (less impact on perf but affects token count). For the triage flows we often recommend a smaller curated model + aggressive caching.
[02:45] Jordan Lee: Also routing policies — you can route high-priority requests to dedicated and lower priority to hosted. That gives you cost controls while keeping SLOs for critical users.
[02:55] Carlos Mendez: Makes sense. For the POC we want to run representative workloads — about 50 concurrent agents, average 20 tokens per response, peak bursts of 200 concurrent. Can Redwood simulate that in the benchmark?
[03:06] Priya Nair: Yes, that's exactly what we want to validate. We'll need your prompt set and sample concurrency profile. We can run both hosted and dedicated configs across the same workload and produce latency/cost per 1k tokens and throughput curves.
[03:20] Sophie Grant: We'll prepare the prompts. One ask: can you run the benchmark from our region (eu-west-1) to account for region-specific latency?
[03:27] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We'll schedule runs in eu-west-1. For dedicated we can provision a short reserved pool for the window.
[03:34] Jordan Lee: Scheduling note — we propose Tue 2026-02-24 14:00-16:00 UTC for the benchmark window, pending your infra readiness.
[03:41] Carlos Mendez: That works for us if we can get KMS done before then.
[03:45] Anita Rao: Security still needs the key policy and we want to review the SOC2 artifact. Also audit logging — will Redwood push audit logs back to our Splunk?
[03:55] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can integrate via our audit log forwarding to your S3 or Splunk— we provide options. We'll include the setup instructions in the security pack.
[04:05] Priya Nair: Quick callout on data retention: hosted endpoints default to short retention; for Private we can configure retention policy that meets regulated PII rules. We'll document retention settings for your compliance review.
[04:16] Liam O'Connor: On the networking side we have one more thing — do you require TCP keepalive settings tuned? We saw a few early disconnects during health checks.
[04:24] Priya Nair: We recommend a 60s keepalive for long-lived streams; we'll add that note to the runbook.
[04:29] Jordan Lee: Ok — let's go through the infra checklist quickly so we all align. Priya?
[04:34] Priya Nair: Infra checklist: VPC peering established (yes), service account created and IAM role attached (yes, pending RBAC mapping), KMS key created and grant for Redwood (pending), firewall and egress rules allow TCP 443 to Redwood egress IPs (done), sample prompts uploaded to S3 and shared with Redwood (pending from Nexa), Splunk/S3 audit destination configured (optional).
[04:55] Carlos Mendez: We'll finish the RBAC and KMS by Friday EOD. Sophie will share prompts tomorrow.
[05:01] Sophie Grant: Yep, I'll put them in the S3 bucket and send the link after this call. Expect 500 prompts, mix of short/long/structured requests.
[05:09] Priya Nair: Great, that should be sufficient for a representative run. On the perf side, I want to flag that the initial hosted numbers had a synthetic bias — we saw slightly elevated token times due to cold KV cache; in production with your prefix patterns the effective cost will be lower. We'll instrument the benchmark to replicate warm and cold flows.
[05:27] Liam O'Connor: For the canary — do you have guidance on rollout percentages? We want to avoid big blasts if something behaves oddly.
[05:33] Jordan Lee: Standard practice is a 5% canary for 1 hour, then 25% for 2 hours, then full if everything looks good. Redwood's Console will surface latency and error spikes and allow automatic rollback. We'll add the canary playbook to the runbook.
[05:46] Anita Rao: One more thing from security — can Redwood sign an NDA addendum for KMS handling? We have a template.
[05:51] Jordan Lee: Yes, legal can sign. I'll attach the NDA addendum with the security pack.
[05:55] Carlos Mendez: Perfect. Anything from pricing — Jordan?
[06:00] Jordan Lee: We'll send an updated pricing note that includes the pilot estimate (two-week dedicated short-term) and hosted per-token estimates. For procurement we'll include the T&Cs and enterprise contract template.
[06:10] Sophie Grant: If we see the benchmark numbers align, timeline to production — about 4-6 weeks?
[06:16] Priya Nair: That's reasonable: finalize infra and keys week 1, benchmark & tune week 2, small canary + validation week 3, ramp week 4. If anything blocks we'll surface it immediately.
[06:28] Carlos Mendez: Ok, that sounds like a plan.
[06:31] Jordan Lee: Quick recap of action items — I'll send the security pack and SOC2 docs; Priya will share the runbook and perf matrix; Liam and Carlos to complete KMS and RBAC; Sophie to upload prompts. We'll aim for the benchmark on 2026-02-24.
[06:46] Sophie Grant: Thanks all.
[06:48] Anita Rao: Thanks.
[06:50] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the links.
[07:00] [call ends]
